findings.quote: The vendor's peer set includes AEP, DUK, SO, NEE and VST, but no comparable multiples sit on the grounding surface, so a formal peer comparison is pending a peer data source.
findings.issue: The named peer set is not on the grounding surface. The prompt Facts block only carries 'Multiples (company column; peers pending a peer data source)' with no tickers, and the report's own multiples note says 'Peer multiples pending a peer data source.' Naming AEP, DUK, SO, NEE and VST is a recalled-from-memory claim (rubric 2). It is also factually wrong: the FactPack peer set is AEP, CWEN, DUK and GEV. The sentence contradicts itself by naming a specific peer set while saying no peer data sits on the surface.
findings.fix: Remove the specific tickers. State only that a peer set and comparable multiples are not on the grounding surface and that a formal peer comparison is pending a peer data source.
findings.note: Still fixed in the rewrite. multiplesCommentary reads 'The pack carries no peer multiples, so we anchor on the company's own multiples and consensus EPS rather than on a peer premium or discount.' No peer or competitor is named anywhere in the judgment.

findings.quote: Delivery against the consensus FY27E revenue of $36.4B and EPS of $12.13 and $13.25 that frame the growth outlook.
findings.issue: The period label is wrong for one EPS figure. Per the Estimates block, $12.13 is the FY26E EPS and only $13.25 is the FY27E EPS ($36.4B is FY27E revenue). Filing both EPS numbers under 'FY27E' attaches $12.13 to the wrong period (rubric 1/3); a reader parses both EPS as FY27E.
findings.fix: Label the periods explicitly, e.g. 'consensus FY27E revenue of $36.4B, with EPS of $12.13 (FY26E) and $13.25 (FY27E),' or drop the FY26E EPS from this FY27E pointer.
findings.note: Still fixed. catalysts[4] is now a margin-recovery pointer, and every EPS figure in the rewrite carries its period ('Consensus EPS of $12.13 for FY26E and $13.25 for FY27E' in analystCommentary; the scenario drivers label FY26E and FY27E correctly).

findings.quote: Ownership is concentrated among institutions: The Vanguard Group at 11.7%, BlackRock at 7.2%, ECP ControlCo at 7.0% in a Schedule 13G filed January 14, 2026, State Street at 5.7% and Capital International Investors at 5.5%.
findings.issue: Stale holdings presented as current (rubric 3). Per the proxy footnotes, Vanguard's 11.7% comes from a Schedule 13G/A filed February 13, 2024 as of December 29, 2023, and BlackRock's 7.2% from a 13G/A filed January 26, 2024 as of December 29, 2023. Only ECP's stake (January 14, 2026) was dated; Vanguard's and BlackRock's were shown undated as if current concentration.
findings.fix: Date the stale holders, noting Vanguard's and BlackRock's percentages are from the December 2023 13G/A filings, or flag that the >5% holder table mixes 2023-vintage 13G/A data with the January 2026 ECP filing rather than presenting a single current snapshot.
findings.note: Still fixed. insiderOwnership reads 'The Vanguard Group (11.7%) and BlackRock (7.2%) are shown as of December 29, 2023 per Schedule 13G/A filings, while ECP ControlCo, LLC (7.0%) is shown as of January 14, 2026 per a Schedule 13G,' and flags that the State Street and Capital International footnotes are not captured.

findings.quote: the shares already trade about 36% below their 52-week high of $412.70, which shows how quickly that premium can move.
findings.issue: The '~36% below the 52-week high of $412.70' claim was stated in full in at least four places: analystCommentary, sections.executiveSummary.thesis, sections.finalRecommendation.body[0] and here in sections.risks.systemic (the Base scenario driver also cited the $412.70 high). Rubric 7 asks that a figure be introduced once and referred back in words; this was the same claim repeated across sections rather than pointed to.
findings.fix: State the 36% / $412.70 figure once (thesis) and refer back in words elsewhere without repeating the number in every section.
findings.note: Still fixed. The $412.70 high appears once, in the thesis ('far below the 52-week high of $412.70 and nearer the low'); risks.systemic no longer cites the price fall. The 52-week low is a separate repetition, logged under F-17.

findings.quote: The proxy describes pay-for-performance practices: a majority of NEO pay is variable cash and equity, incentive awards are capped and subject to clawback, change-in-control benefits use double-trigger vesting, and there are no employment agreements with the CEO or NEOs, no hedging or pledging of company stock, and no option repricing without stockholder approval.
findings.issue: The governance paragraph catalogued proxy facts (board independence, the pay-practice list, no related-party transactions) but reached no view the reader can act on (rubric 4). The neighbouring leadership, capitalAllocation and insiderOwnership subfields each interpret; governance only listed.
findings.fix: Add a reading of what this governance profile means for a minority holder — e.g. that full board/committee independence plus capped, clawback-subject, double-trigger pay design tempers agency risk around a large, dilutive acquisition.
findings.note: Still fixed. governance closes with 'For outside holders this is a clean profile that lowers agency risk, though it does not by itself make a large acquisition a good use of capital.'

findings.quote: Power and fuel price exposure: the 10-K states earnings and cash flows vary with spot and forward power prices, and baseload nuclear can see negative pricing when supply exceeds demand.
findings.issue: The executive-summary risk pointers stated the full substance rather than pointing, and sections.risks.idiosyncratic then repeated it under the same lead labels (rubric 7 paraphrase): 'Power and fuel price exposure' vs idiosyncratic[1]; 'Calpine integration and dilution' vs idiosyncratic[0]; 'Nuclear fuel supply' vs idiosyncratic[3] all carried near-identical 10-K content in two places.
findings.fix: Make the executive-summary risks one-line pointers ('commodity-price exposure; see Risks') and let the idiosyncratic section carry the mechanism and what-to-watch.
findings.note: Still fixed. All five executive-summary risks are one-line pointers ('Power and fuel price exposure; see Risks.', 'Thin margins on the enlarged revenue base; see Financials.'), and the 10-K detail sits only in risks.idiosyncratic.

findings.quote: Its 10-Q for the period ended 2026-06-30 describes a fleet of 55 gigawatts spanning nuclear, natural gas, oil, geothermal, hydro, wind and solar
findings.issue: ISO-format dates in prose (rubric 9). '2026-06-30' appeared here and in analystCommentary ('period ended 2026-06-30' and 'as of 2026-09-22'), where house style calls for prose dates.
findings.fix: Render dates in prose form, e.g. 'its 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026' and 'as of September 22, 2026'.
findings.note: Still fixed. A scan of the rewritten judgment finds no YYYY-MM-DD dates; companyOverview and analystCommentary use 'June 30, 2026' and 'September 22, 2026'.

findings.quote: the Pastoria Solar Project and Power Bank sit in California under a 15-year PPA with Pacific Gas and Electric Company.
findings.issue: Wrong counterparty for the solar project (rubric 1/2). The MD&A states the 105 MW Pastoria Solar Project is 'the largest renewable energy project contracted by the California Department of Water Resources,' while only the Pastoria Power Bank is 'contracted and supported by a 15-year power purchase agreement with Pacific Gas and Electric Company.' The body attached the 15-year PG&E PPA to the Solar Project as well, which the pack does not support.
findings.fix: Attribute the 15-year PG&E PPA to the Pastoria Power Bank only, and note the Solar Project is contracted by the California Department of Water Resources.
findings.note: Still fixed. segments[0].body reads 'the Pastoria Solar Project is contracted by the California Department of Water Resources, and the co-located Pastoria Power Bank carries a 15-year power purchase agreement with Pacific Gas and Electric Company.'

findings.quote: Our target range of $290 to $350 brackets the base case and sits below the Street's consensus target, reflecting the commodity sensitivity and integration risk that temper an otherwise constructive demand story.
findings.issue: Precision slip (rubric 6). The prose says the '$290 to $350' band 'sits below the Street's consensus target,' but the Street consensus target on the grounding surface is $348.55, and the band's top of $350 is $1.45 above it. The below-consensus point holds for the probability-weighted fair value (~$299) and the base case ($300) but not for the full stated band, so applying 'sits below' to the range as written is inaccurate at the top. analystCommentary and thesis correctly frame this against the fair value ('below the Street's $348.55 consensus target'); only scenarioCommentary extends the claim to the range.
findings.fix: Attach the below-consensus claim to the base case / fair value rather than the whole band (e.g. 'the band brackets the base case, and our fair value sits below the Street's consensus target of $348.55'), or note the top of the range is essentially at consensus.
findings.note: The quoted sentence is gone, but the slip moved to valuation.multiplesCommentary: 'Our range tops out near the consensus and the median rather than above them.' The $350 top is above the $348.55 consensus (below only the $350.50 median). The same range-vs-consensus point is also made in the thesis ('our target range tops out near the Street's $348.55 consensus target'); keep it there and drop the multiplesCommentary sentence.

findings.quote: On the figures alone, revenue has grown faster than profit since the deal closed.
findings.issue: Contradicted by the surface (rubric 2). The deal closed January 7, 2026, and the same paragraph cites six-month GAAP net income attributable to common shareholders of $2,103 million versus $957 million, more than double. Revenue cannot have grown faster: Q2 revenue rose +23.0% and the FY26E step-up is +38%. The trailing operating margin of 14.7% is also above FY25's 12.1%. Only the second quarter shows profit lagging revenue. The same one-quarter reading is generalised in sections.executiveSummary.thesis.body ('margins on the enlarged revenue base stay thin') and sections.finalRecommendation.body[0..1] ('Margins on the larger revenue base are thin so far').
findings.fix: Limit the claim to the second quarter, e.g. 'In the second quarter, revenue grew while profit fell; the six-month figures point the other way, and the pack does not explain either.' In the thesis and finalRecommendation.body[1], say margins were thin 'in the second quarter' rather than 'so far' or on 'the enlarged revenue base', and name the stronger six-month and trailing figures as the counter-reading.

findings.quote: Most output is still sold at market prices, so the fleet's earnings move with power and fuel prices (see Risks).
findings.issue: Unsupported quantification (rubric 2). Nothing on the surface says how much output is sold at market prices versus hedged or contracted. The 10-K says earnings are exposed to 'the unhedged portion of our generation portfolio' and that wholesale generators use retail operations to hedge output, which moatFactors[2] cites. The same unsupported 'most' recurs in sections.businessMoat.durability ('most near-term earnings remain merchant, because the long-term nuclear PPAs start in 2029 and later'). This claim is the stated main reason for the NARROW rating.
findings.fix: Use the 10-K's own framing: earnings and cash flows are exposed to spot and forward prices on the unhedged portion of the portfolio, and the new long-term nuclear PPAs do not start until 2029 through 2032. Drop 'most' in both places, or say the pack does not show the contracted share.

findings.quote: In ERCOT the company owns the Freestone and Pin Oak Creek assets and is selling the Brazos Valley Energy Center.
findings.issue: The 10-Q places Pin Oak Creek ('the ERCOT grid') and Brazos Valley ('in ERCOT') in ERCOT. It places the Freestone Energy Center only 'in Freestone County, Texas' and never names its market. Putting Freestone in ERCOT is an inference the source invites but does not make (rubric 2). The fact is low-stakes, but the desk rule is not to recall.
findings.fix: Say 'In Texas the company has the Freestone Energy Center and the Pin Oak Creek Energy Center, which serves the ERCOT grid, and is selling the Brazos Valley Energy Center in ERCOT,' or drop Freestone from the ERCOT sentence.

findings.quote: Power prices soften, the 2029/2030 PJM auction clears toward the $175/MW-day floor, and Calpine proves costly and dilutive, as the 10-K warns it may. EPS stalls at the FY26E consensus of $12.13 instead of reaching the FY27E consensus
findings.issue: The Bear's number does not match its story (rubrics 5 and 6). The story has softer power prices and a costly, dilutive Calpine, yet EPS still lands on the full FY26E consensus of $12.13, up from FY25's $7.40. The only downside priced is the missed FY27E increase plus a lower multiple. A Bear that keeps the current-year consensus whole while saying the deal disappoints is close to a formality on the earnings side. The ADI review hit the same problem: a Bear held EPS steady while its story said the cycle turns.
findings.fix: Make the EPS basis match the story. Either price EPS below the FY26E consensus, describe the shortfall in words, and re-derive the Bear price and label from that, or narrow the story to a pure de-rating and drop 'dilutive' and the power-price softening. Then argue the 25% weight on the Bear as rewritten.

findings.quote: Consensus FY26E revenue of $35.1B, a {+ +38% +} step-up over FY25, includes Calpine from January 7, and the second-quarter revenue rise (see Financials) shows that step-up arriving
findings.issue: Two problems. (1) Q2 revenue rose +23.0% with Calpine in the quarter, well short of the +38% full-year step-up, so the quarter does not show the step-up arriving. It is a gap the rest of the year must close (rubric 2). (2) No source says what the consensus includes; 'includes Calpine from January 7' is the author's inference. The gap also matters for the calls: the Base driver says consensus FY26E revenue of $35.1B is 'broadly met' and never names the Q2 shortfall against that pace as a counter-case (rubric 5).
findings.fix: Say Q2 growth of +23.0% ran below the +38% step-up that consensus FY26E implies, and frame the consensus as reflecting the enlarged company without asserting its composition. Name that shortfall once, as the counter-case to the Base case's revenue assumption.

findings.quote: PJM capacity pricing supports the near-term outlook: in July 2026 the entire RTO cleared the 2028/2029 Base Residual Auction at the $325/MW-day price cap, including all submitted CEG units.
findings.issue: Period mismatch (rubric 3/6). The MD&A presents 2028/2029 as a delivery year, so this capacity price applies from 2028 onward. That is not near-term, and it lies beyond the FY27E EPS that the scenarios price. The Base driver (sections.valuation.scenarios[1].driver) also leans on it: 'the 2028/2029 auction result at the cap supports capacity revenue' sits beside an FY27E EPS anchor. growth.points[5] calls the 2029 PPAs late, but the report treats a 2028/2029 price as near-term.
findings.fix: Say the auction result supports capacity revenue for the 2028/2029 delivery year, after the FY27E horizon. Remove it from the Base case's support for the FY27E EPS path, or say it bears on value beyond FY27E rather than on FY27E earnings.

findings.quote: We would move to HOLD if the price rose toward the low end of our range without new evidence, because on these scenarios expected upside falls below the BUY threshold well before the price reaches the low end of our range
findings.issue: The trigger is not where the page's own math flips the label (rubric 6; see the ADI F-25 lesson). With a $298.75 fair value and a $205 Bear, reward/risk falls below 0.50x at a price only a few dollars above $263.46, about a 1.5% rise. Expected upside falls below +10% at about a 3% rise. The $290 low end is far away. The sentence also names expected upside as the binding test, but reward/risk fails first. As written, a reader would expect the BUY to hold until the price nears $290, and it does not.
findings.fix: Without quoting a computed price, say that on these scenarios a rise of a few percent from $263.46 would derive HOLD, with reward/risk falling below 0.50x first. Then drop the 'toward the low end of our range' framing.

findings.quote: Its 10-Q for the period ended June 30, 2026 describes a fleet of 55 gigawatts after the January 2026 Calpine acquisition
findings.issue: Several cases of the same sentence or claim in two or more sections (rubric 7). (1) This sentence opener also appears in sections.executiveSummary.companyOverview ('Its 10-Q for the period ended June 30, 2026 describes a fleet of 55 gigawatts across...'). (2) 'Consensus FY26E revenue of $35.1B, a +38% step-up over FY25' is in both financials.incomeCommentary and growth.points[0]. (3) The Q2 thin-margin and net-income-fall story is told in analystCommentary, thesis.body, incomeCommentary, management.leadership, growth.points[0], scenarioCommentary and finalRecommendation.body[1]. (4) 'Bear ... below the 52-week low' appears in analystCommentary and scenarioCommentary, and 'real/genuine downside, not a formality' in scenarioCommentary and finalRecommendation.body[1]. (5) 'moderate BUY' is in analystCommentary and finalRecommendation.body[1]. (6) 'all submitted CEG units' cleared at the cap appears in segments[0].body and growth.points[4].
findings.fix: Keep the 55 GW sentence in companyOverview only. Keep the $35.1B/+38% figure in one place, and point to it in words elsewhere. Argue the Q2 margin and net-income point in incomeCommentary, and elsewhere point to it in a clause ('see Financials'). State the 52-week-low and 'real downside' points once, in scenarioCommentary. Say 'moderate BUY' once. Drop the auction detail from segments[0].body.

findings.quote: New capacity in service, including the Pin Oak Creek Energy Center and the Pastoria Power Bank, which came online in July 2026.
findings.issue: Both events happened before the September 22, 2026 report date: Pin Oak Creek reached commercial operation in April 2026 and the Power Bank came online in July 2026. A completed event is not a forward catalyst.
findings.fix: Make it forward-looking, e.g. 'Earnings contribution from capacity that entered service in 2026 (Pin Oak Creek, Pastoria Power Bank) in coming quarters.'

findings.quote: We own the shares for per-share earnings rather than revenue.
findings.issue: Voice (rubric 9). 'We own the shares' implies the desk holds a position; the intended point is that the case rests on per-share earnings. Also, in sections.valuation.multiplesCommentary, 'Because trailing net margin is 11.1%, the sales multiple says little on its own' is a non sequitur. A positive 11.1% margin does not make P/S uninformative.
findings.fix: Write 'The case rests on per-share earnings rather than revenue.' In multiplesCommentary, say plainly that the case is valued on earnings because consensus EPS is the quantity the scenarios price, or drop the sentence.
